response: Yes, radiotherapy around the time of pregnancy for Hodgkin's disease may modify the risk of breast cancer. Women who receive radiation therapy, especially at a young age, are at an increased risk of developing breast cancer. Pregnancy at the time of radiation exposure may not significantly alter this risk. In fact, studies suggest that radiation exposure during pregnancy may still increase the risk of breast cancer, although the risk may be lower compared to radiation exposure outside of pregnancy. However, more research is needed to fully understand the relationship between radiation therapy during pregnancy and breast cancer risk.
